chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him how tayammum is performed, so he placed his hand upon the earth and wiped with it his face and his forearms up to the elbows.

So the correct approach regarding this report is that we carry it upon a form of taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrines of the generality. And it has been said in its interpretation that what is intended by it is the ruling, not the act, because when he wipes the outer side of the palm, it is as though he washed his forearms in wudu (ablution), and thus by wiping the two palms in tayammum he attains the legal effect of washing the two forearms in wudu (ablution).

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under particular circumstances
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: dry ablution performed with earth when wudu (ablution) cannot be done
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal ruling or effect intended by the report
key_terms.الْفِعْلُ: the outward act or literal physical performance
key_terms.الْكَفَّيْنِ: the two palms or hands, whose wiping is central to tayammum
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقَيْنِ: the two elbows, the stated upper limit in the report
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), used here as the point of legal analogy
key_terms.ذِرَاعَيْهِ: his forearms, mentioned here up to the elbows

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith about wiping the forearms to the elbows in tayammum understood in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report discusses the manner of tayammum and then addresses how a narration mentioning wiping up to the elbows should be understood. The explanation presents it either as a case of taqiyyah or as referring to legal effect rather than the literal act, situating the report within juristic interpretation in Shia hadith scholarship.
